report.summary: This change should not merge: it makes issue paging skip one item. Head commit d3a1f12 changes the `nextOffset` returned by `page()` (used by the list_issues and list_issue_comments agent tools) to `offset + bounded.length + 1`. But `offset` is passed straight to SQL `.offset(start)` with `.limit(50)` in apps/tempo/src/artifacts/issues.ts, so it is a zero-based item index. The next unread item is at `offset + bounded.length`, and the +1 drops it on every page boundary. This breaks the spec's promise in docs/09 that following `nextOffset` until it is null lists every entry. The existing worker test `expect(first.nextOffset).toBe(2)` now fails: the result is 3, and the second page holds 1 item instead of 2. The spec was not changed, and docs/IMPLEMENTATION_NOTES.md was not updated.

findings.text: Off-by-one in `nextOffset`: one item is skipped every time an agent follows it. With 4 comments where the first page holds 2 (because of the byte limit), `nextOffset` becomes 3, so the second call runs SQL OFFSET 3 and never returns the comment at index 2. It also happens when there is no byte limit: a full page of 50 from offset 0 now points to 51, which skips item 50.

evidence.quote: nextOffset: bounded.length < items.length || items.length === 50 ? offset + bounded.length + 1 : null,
evidence.why: The store uses the offset as a zero-based SQL OFFSET (`const start = validateOffset(offset);` … `.limit(50)` `.offset(start)` in apps/tempo/src/artifacts/issues.ts). The first item not yet returned is therefore at `offset + bounded.length`. Adding 1 skips it, which breaks docs/09: "follow `nextOffset` until it is null, even when a page contains fewer than 50 entries."

findings.text: The existing worker test for this behavior contradicts the change, and the change does not update it. With the new code, `first.nextOffset` is 3. The second page then holds 1 item, so the checks `toHaveLength(2)` and the 4-distinct-ids set check also fail. CLAUDE.md rule 15 requires `bun run test` to pass.

evidence.why: 4 comments of 65000 NUL characters each produce a first page of 2 items under the MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES limit. The head code returns 0 + 2 + 1 = 3, not 2.

checked.risk: Real contracts: offset semantics of the store/SQL layer the tool output feeds back into
The spec: docs/09 says to follow nextOffset until it is null, and the change does not update the spec
Tests: whether the existing pagination test still holds
Failure paths, idempotency, security, build environment: not affected by this one-expression change (read-only listing, and no change to auth, secrets or the image)
